summary: Jason Matthew McCombs is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned a B.S. at the University of Michigan and a PhD at UCLA under Gregory Schopen, where he later served as a lecturer.

Jason Neelis works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at the University of Texas and earned his PhD at the University of Washington. His posts include the University of Washington, University of Florida, and Wilfrid Laurier University.

Jason Protass specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He earned his PhD at Stanford University under John Kieschnick and held research posts at Ryukoku University (~2013–2014) and Academia Sinica (~2014–2015).

Jay Holt Valentine specializes in Tibetology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Delaware, Naropa University, and the University of Virginia, completing his PhD at Virginia (~2007–2013) under Kurtis R. Schaeffer.

Jay Jasanoff is a linguist and Indologist who studied at Harvard University (~1963–1968). He held academic appointments at the University of California, Berkeley (~1972–1978), Cornell University (~1978–1998), and Harvard University (~1998).

Jay L. Garfield works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He has held positions at Hampshire College, Smith College, the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, the University of Melbourne, the University of Massachusetts Amherst, and the National University of Singapore.

Jayandra Soni is a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. He earned PhDs from Banaras Hindu University and McMaster University, and served as a lecturer in Indology and Tibetology at the University of Marburg (~1991–2012).
Jaś Elsner is a scholar in history, archaeology, and religious studies. He has held posts at the University of Michigan and the University of Chicago (~2013).
Jean Dantinne is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Étienne Lamotte. He held a post as a librarian at the University of Liège.

Jean Filliozat was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at INALCO (~1930–1935). He served as a professor at the Collège de France (1951–1978) and as director of the École française d'Extrême-Orient (~1956–1977).

Jean Philippe Vogel was an Indologist and archaeologist who studied at the University of Amsterdam (~1890–1897). He served with the Archaeological Survey of India (1910–1911) and as Director at Leiden University (1914–1939).

Jean Przyluski was an Indologist, linguist, and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the EPHE (~1914–1920). He held posts at INALCO (1923), the EPHE (~1926–1931), and the Collège de France (~1931–1944).

Jean-Baptiste Biot was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Sinology. He studied at Collège Louis-le-Grand, École polytechnique, and École Nationale des Ponts et Chaussées, later holding posts at the Collège de France and the Science Faculty of Paris.
Jean-François Jarrige was an archaeologist and Indologist. He studied at the Lycée Claude Fauriel and the École du Louvre, and served as the head of the Musée Guimet (~1986–2008).
Jean-François Revel was a philosopher who studied at the Lycée Jean-Baptiste-Say, the Lycée du Parc (~1941–1943), and the École Normale Supérieure (1943).

Jean-Louis Burnouf was a linguist who studied at Collège d'Harcourt and under Antoine-Léonard de Chézy. He held positions at the École Normale Supérieure (~1810–1826), the University of Paris (~1811–1844), and the Collège de France (1817–1844).

Jean-Luc Achard is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1993–1999) and held a post at the Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique (~2003).
Jean-Luc Chevillard is a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He studied at the École Normale Supérieure (1975) and became a researcher at the Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique (~1991).

Jean-Noël Robert specializes in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. He studied at INALCO under Bernard Frank, later holding posts at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1990–2011) and the Collège de France (2011–2022).
Jean-Pierre Abel-Rémusat was a scholar in Sinology and linguistics who studied at INALCO. He held the chair in Chinese at the Collège de France from 1814 until 1832.
